text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The balloting of shares in Fumakilla (Malaysia) Bhd, which is coming up for listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, has been postponed indefinitely by the Securities Commission. The regulatory watchdog did not explain the reasons for its decision.

- Hock Hua (Sabah) Bank Bhd, now the target of a takeover by parties linked to the financial adviser to the Malaysian government, Daim Zainuddin, is likely to be injected into UCM Industrial Corporation Bhd's stockbroking arm.

- Malaysia is satisfied with the revised wording of the leaders' declaration on the Information Technology Agreement which provides flexibility and is not binding upon its members, said Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad

- Padiaberas Nasional Bhd (Bernas) expects to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in May next year. Bernas is currently a governmental body overseeing the production and stockpiling of rice in Malaysia.

- Renong Bhd is among five companies shortlisted to bid for a portion of the $450 million (1.1 billion ringgit) highway project in the state of Maharashtra in India, said Works Minister S. Samy Vellu.

- The Securities Commission has directed Trans Capital Holdings Bhd to postpone the balloting of its shares indefinitely. The balloting was originally due to be held next Wednesday. No reason was given for the decision.
- Hock Hua Bank Bhd, whose subsidiary Hock Hua Bank (Sabah) Bhd is up for sale, will be cash richer to the extent of 200 million ringgit after the disposal.

- Syarikat Telefon Wireless (M) Sdn Bhd, which operates radio-based telecommunications services, is targetting the capture of at least five percent of a projected four million new customers by the year 2000.
- Transwater Corp Bhd has formed a strategic alliance with Lyonnaise (South East Asia) Sdn Bhd for the joint development of projects in the drinking water industry in Malaysia.
